newsitem.title: UK: BT says didn't deliberately mislead customers.
newsitem.headline: BT says didn't deliberately mislead customers.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc responded to industry watchdog Oftel's criticism of what the company says to customers about competitors and said it was committed to trading fairly.
In a statement, BT said: "BT is committed to trading vigorously and fairly...we never set out deliberately to mislead customers."

But it conceded that "there have been occasional lapses by our people when discussing what can be very complicated issues," and said it had strengthened its team dealing with inquiries about competitors on September 2.
"As soon as we became aware of the few reported lapses we put action in hand to revise training and other procedures," BT said.
Oftel director general Don Cruickshank said earlier on Tuesday that he was "dismayed" that BT had not shown "a culture ...in which competing fairly is instinctive to its staff."

Oftel's concerns were raised by the Consumers' Association, which submitted tapes of interviews with BT staff in shops and on telephone inquiry numbers, the majority of which were "unsatisfactory from a fair trading point of view."

Oftel issued an order asking BT to behave fairly when talking about competitors. BT said the evidence from the CA "would not stand up in court," slamming it as "surreptiously made," and claiming many questions were "deliberately designed to confuse."
